meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'влекаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'get carried away'.

examples.trans: Lyova, do not get carried away with pancakes.

examples.text: Это слово «увлекаться» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'get carried away' is often heard in conversation.

examples.text: Тогда положите мне ещё парочку блинов!
examples.trans: Then serve me a couple more pancakes!

examples.text: Большое спасибо вам за вкусные блины.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for the delicious pancakes.
Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

meanings.note: takes the accusative; everyday synonym of о

examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?
I'm asking for the last time.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'test, analysis' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это слово «анализ» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'test' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ровень'). Common masculine noun meaning 'level' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cholesterol' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мой уровень холестерина был почти в норме.
examples.trans: My cholesterol level was almost in range.

examples.text: Это слово «холестерин» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'cholesterol' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'almost, nearly' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Наш с вами город очень старый. Почти четыре века здесь были набеги.
examples.trans: Our town is very old. For almost four centuries there were raids here.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'norm, good shape' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мой уровень холестерина был почти в норме.
examples.trans: My cholesterol level was almost in range.

зайти.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.en: to come in, to step in

examples.trans: I'll drop by in the evening.

examples.text: Ну, как хочешь. Лидия Алексеевна, зайдите, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Well, as you like. Lidia Alekseyevna, come in, please!

meanings.note: Agent noun formed with the international suffix '-ист' denoting a specialist or adherent. Common feminine noun meaning 'dry cleaner’s' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Зайди в химчистку и возьми мой костюм.
examples.trans: Go to the dry cleaners and take my suit.

examples.text: Это слово «химчистка» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'dry cleaner’s' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: 'взять на работу' = to give someone a job
'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.

examples.trans: This is my wedding suit, actually!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

успевать.gloss: to manage in time, have time

meanings.en: to manage in time, have enough time

examples.trans: We cannot get anything done in time.

examples.text: Повара ничего не успевают вовремя отдавать.
examples.trans: The cooks cannot serve anything on time.

examples.text: Я не успеваю. Это в другую сторону.
examples.trans: I do not have time. That is the other way.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: с другой стороны = on the other hand

examples.trans: On the other hand, it's interesting.
The shop is on that side.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'слуга'). Common feminine noun meaning 'service, favor' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I don't forget favors like that.

examples.text: Я такие важные услуги никогда не забываю.
examples.trans: I never forget such important services.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'решать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'allow, permit'.

examples.text: Ты мне костюм, а я разрешаю опоздать.
examples.trans: You get me the suit, and I allow you to be late.

examples.text: Сегодня тебе разрешат играть со всеми игрушками.
examples.trans: Today they will let you play with all toys.

meanings.note: + на: опоздать на работу = be late for work
almost always the short form: я согласен (man), я согласна (woman)

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').

examples.trans: Look what the conditions are like here.

examples.text: Посмотрите, какие тут условия. В эту комнату, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Look what the conditions are like here. Into this room, please.
We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'у-шеф'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sous-chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Are you a sous-chef or who?

examples.text: Тащи свою птицу су-шефу на стол!
examples.trans: Drag your bird to the sous-chef's table!

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

examples.text: Вика, так нельзя поступать со мной!
examples.trans: Vika, you cannot treat me like this!

examples.text: Я всегда стараюсь поступать честно, как он.
examples.trans: I always try to act honestly, like him.

examples.text: Я не понимаю, почему они так поступают.
examples.trans: I do not understand why they act like that.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

марш.gloss: march! (military command: шагом марш! = forward march!)

meanings.note: Core Russian interj meaning 'march! (military command: шагом марш! = forward march!)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Встала и мыть посуду, шагом марш!
examples.trans: Get up and wash the dishes, forward march!
Off to sleep quickly, march to bed!

examples.text: Пока ещё на мои деньги куплен! Встала и мыть посуду, шагом марш!
examples.trans: It's still bought with my money! Get up and wash the dishes, forward march!

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'собка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'back room, storage room' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это слово «подсобка» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'back room' is often heard in conversation.
